item.title: Chemistry Seminar Presented by Prof. J.R Schmidt (University of Wisconsin–Madison)Title: Modulating the selectivity of electrocatalytic reduction in solution — Tue Oct 20, 11:40 AM — French Family Science Center 2237
item.description:
The Department of Chemistry is excited to host Prof. J.R Schmidt on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, at 11:40 am for a departmental seminar.
Title: Modulating the selectivity of electrocatalytic reduction in solution
Abstract: Achieving selectivity toward a single target product is a major hurdle in electrochemical synthesis, particularly for complex reactants. Focusing first on selective 2e⁻ oxygen reduction to hydrogen peroxide, I will show how computational modeling guided the design of novel, stable metal-compound electrocatalysts and enabled microkinetic analysis of the competing 2e⁻ and 4e⁻ pathways.
To learn more about Prof. J.R Schmidt research, please visit: https://schmidt.chem.wisc.edu/
Seminar hosted by Prof. Weitao Yang
Source: Duke University

item.title: Lester Horton Technique Workshop with Melvin Sutton — Tue Oct 20, 6:30 PM — Empower School of Movement
item.description:
Developed by pioneering American dancer and choreographer Lester Horton, Horton technique is a codified modern dance practice designed to strengthen, stretch, and awaken the entire body. Its vocabulary emphasizes anatomical alignment, flexibility, balance, coordination, lateral movement, spatial clarity, and full-bodied physical expression. During this 90-minute workshop, Sutton will guide participants through a structured Horton-based practice that connects technical discipline with musicality, groundedness, physicality, and authentic artistic expression. Dancers will explore how the technique builds the strength and versatility required across modern, contemporary, and concert dance practices.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Fri Jan 15 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Fri Jan 15, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

The exhibition is a speculative, immersive world-building study that invites guests to explore (geo)locating self and home amid a rapidly and frequently changing post-pandemic “new” world. It will be on display in the art gallery at the African American Cultural Center from Oct. 28, 2026, to Feb. 28, 2027. A behind-the-scenes look at the exhibition is set for Nov. 11.

item.title: NC Public Librarian Certification Commission — Fri Jan 15, 10:30 AM — DNCR
item.description:
The NC Public Librarian Certification Commission was formed in 1936 to set minimum standards for public librarians to protect and maintain public library resources, to assure professional management and administration of library services, to meet the personnel requirements for State Aid administered by the Library of NC, and to guarantee the best possible public library service to all North Carolinians.
The North Carolina General Statute 143B-68 states that the commission must be comprised of: the Chairman of the public libraries section of NCLA, two individuals named by the Governor upon nomination of the NCLA, the dean of a State or regionally accredited graduate school of librarianship in North Carolina appointed by the Governor, and one member at large appointed by the Governor. Commission members appointed by the Governor serve 4-year terms, all others serve 2-year terms.

item.description:
FEATURING
earspace
earspace is an ensemble consisting of violin, viola, cello, flute, oboe, clarinet, piano, and percussion that performs a combination of conducted and unconducted chamber music of a wide variety of scopes. Passionate producers, the ensemble is dedicated to both commissioning new, immersive works and amplifying rarely-performed gems of the repertoire. Founded in North Carolina, the group is now based across the US and performs regularly around the east coast, collaborating with organizations including the Southern Exposure New Music Series, Towson University, Duke University, UNC Chapel Hill, the Peabody Institute, Asheville Ballet, Carolina Performing Arts, and others.
The ensemble seeks to expose the inherent potentials within every moment and space, cultivating visceral reactions unique to every manifestation. Through their projects, they explore the extremities of contemporary performance and work to bring audiences closer to the music they experience.

item.description: 5 Points Gallery is pleased to present Carolina, or Thereabouts, a new exhibition of mixed-media paintings by Featured Artist Jenny Blazing exploring the shifting nature of place through observation, memory, and imagination. item.description: POWER AND NOSTALGIA HAVE A SOUND. This is your chance to listen to select movements from Haydn’s Symphonies No. 47, 63, 73, and 103 paired with the nostalgic call of Mozart’s Posthorn Serenade. Experience the wit, elegance, and imagination of Joseph Haydn through a captivating selection of movements drawn from several of his most beloved symphonies. This unique program highlights Haydn’s remarkable creativity while revealing how even he was not above borrowing from himself, revisiting and reimagining some of his most charming and effective musical ideas. Named for its celebrated posthorn solo, which echoes the call of a traveling mail coach, Mozart’s Posthorn Serenade transports listeners to a world of elegance and festivity. One of Mozart’s most joyful and expansive works, it captures the spirit of celebration and adventure that characterized the young composer at the height of his creative powers. item.title: CEE Seminar - Environmental Relevance in Disinfection Research? Influence of Species, Conformation, and “Lived Experience” on Decay Kinetics of Microbial Contaminants — Mon Oct 19, 12:00 PM — None
item.description: Species/strain diversity (i.e., identity determined by genetics) and physiology or conformation (i.e., functional/physical state determined by "lived experience") have the potential to influence the inactivation or decay kinetics of microbial contaminants, such as bacteria or DNA. Nonetheless, most disinfection research utilizes reference strain organisms or model systems cultivated in the laboratory for experiments used to assess disinfection kinetics, with limited discussion of the environmental relevance of the observed disinfection behavior. To illustrate the importance of identity and lived experience on disinfection kinetics, two examples from research in the Silverman Laboratory will be presented. The first is an evaluation of divergent inactivation kinetics of wastewater-sourced E. coli and enterococci, laboratory-cultured E. coli and three species of Enterococcus with exposure to commonly used disinfectants (i.e., free chlorine, monochloramine, UVC, and simulated sunlight). item.title: Ari Joskowicz: "Money and Memory: How Funding Shaped the Documentation of Jewish History and the Holocaust" — Mon Oct 19, 5:00 PM — Gray 229
item.description:
The Sperling Center for Jewish Studies welcomes Ari Joskowicz, who will give a lecture entitled "Money and Memory: How Funding Shaped the Documentation of Jewish History and the Holocaust." Joskowicz is the Eugene Greener Jr. Chair in Jewish Studies and Professor of Jewish Studies and History at Vanderbilt University, where he also directs the Max Kade Center for European and German Studies. A historian of modern Jewish and European history, his scholarship explores the intersections of Jewish history, minority politics, memory, and the Holocaust, with particular attention to the relationships between Jewish and Romani communities in Europe.
Joskowicz is the author of the award-winning books Rain of Ash: Roma, Jews, and the Holocaust (Princeton University Press, 2023) and The Modernity of Others: Jewish Anti-Catholicism in Germany and France (Stanford University Press, 2014). His research has been recognized with major honors, including the Ernst Fraenkel Prize of the Wiener Library

Masroor is displaying her cycle of original poems as this year's recipient of the C. Eric Lincoln Theology and Arts Fellowship, which provides funding for a Duke student to complete a sacred art project and display it in the Chapel. Her poetry has been published in VOICES Magazine, Muzzle Magazine, the Yale Daily News, and the anthology Without a Doubt: poems illuminating faith. Her poem "Interrupted Connection" received second place in the forty-fourth annual William Carlos William poetry competition.

item.title: Hematology Case Conference: — Tue Oct 20, 8:00 AM — Duke South
item.description:
This weekly conference is held each Tuesday from 8-9 a.m. and includes case-based presentations on a wide variety of topics in hematology. In general, discussion will cover inpatient and outpatient problems, with an emphasis on including primary radiographic data, clinical laboratory results and pathology specimens for review. Several recent articles relevant to the discussion will be presented with each case, with an emphasis on recent research (clinical, translational and basic).
